title: Average Rate of Change of a Quadratic Function
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Find the average rate of change of f(x) = x^2 + 3x over the interval [1, 3], and compute the general difference quotient over [1, 1+h].

steps.title: Evaluate Endpoint Values on [1, 3]
steps.explanation: Substitute the interval endpoints into the function to obtain corresponding y-values.
steps.why: Endpoint function values are required to compute net change Delta y.

steps.title: Compute Average Rate over [1, 3]
steps.explanation: Divide the total vertical change by the horizontal width of the interval.
steps.why: Definition of average rate of change over a closed interval [a, b].

steps.title: Expand f(1 + h) and Form the Difference Quotient
steps.explanation: Substitute 1+h into the quadratic function and expand algebraically.
steps.why: Difference quotient requires evaluating the function at the perturbed coordinate.

steps.title: Simplify the Difference Quotient
steps.explanation: Subtract f(1) = 4, factor out h from the numerator, and cancel the non-zero denominator h.
steps.why: Factoring allows removal of the removable singularity at h = 0.
